title: The Reciprocal Settlement Mesh: a decentralised settlement architecture built from scratch, tested by invariant proof, adversarial attack, shared-shock replay and ablation (pre-registered and hash-locked BEFORE any implementation existed)
why_this_exists: The legacy datasets cannot supply evidence for this system because the system is not in them. The referee report established that the cohort labelled 'risk-sharing' contained only cost-plus sale, lease and forward-purchase contracts -- zero profit-and-loss partnerships. That is evidence of the contradiction in existing practice, not evidence about a decentralised alternative. Mining those files further can only reproduce size-bias and rigged comparisons. So the architecture is specified here from first principles and tested by methods that do not require it to already exist.
terminology_policy: DELIBERATE AND USER-DIRECTED. All operational terms are plain English. The OQM *logic* is retained -- capacity delegated in advance, fidelity owed back, verification decoupled from self-report, unearned capacity inflation as the failure mode -- but no Arabic or theological vocabulary appears anywhere in the specification, the implementation, the results or the tests. This removes a source of reader bias and forces every term to be defined by its measurement rather than by its provenance. A test asserts the absence.
the_simulation_trap_being_avoided: IMPORTANT AND DELIBERATE. A proposed architecture cannot be validated by a simulation whose outcome is written into its own functions. A published JAX cell for this project defines the decentralised arm as D_enc = D_dec = 0.95 (constant) and the centralised arm as D = exp(-0.005*U) with tau = 4.8 + (U/120)^2.5. The collapse of the centralised arm IS the exponential; the stability of the mesh IS the constant. No data enters, and the verdict is fixed by the two function bodies. This is the fifth appearance of the tuned-baseline pattern in this project and it is refused again. Under this specification NO architecture-specific constant may differ between arms: every exogenous input is shared, and the arms may differ ONLY in mechanism. M7 enforces this structurally.
what_can_honestly_be_established_about_a: Not empirical support -- that requires deployment. What CAN be established is four things, and they are what this specification tests: (1) INVARIANTS, proved to hold under every admissible operation, which are theorems rather than observations; (2) ADVERSARIAL RESISTANCE, where an attacker tries to break the mechanism and either succeeds or does not, an outcome the designer does not control; (3) BEHAVIOUR UNDER A SHARED EXOGENOUS SHOCK drawn from real recorded data, with both architectures facing the identical sequence; (4) ABLATION, showing which components carry weight and naming those that do not. None of these is a claim that the system would work in the world. They are the strongest claims available before deployment, and the specification says so.
shock_source: data/colab-audit/banking_dataset.xlsx -- 4,886 real recorded debits with real account balances, committed and hash-pinned. The withdrawal-to-balance ratio of each real debit is replayed as an exogenous liquidity shock. Both architectures face the SAME shock sequence in the SAME order. The shocks are recorded history, not drawn from a fitted distribution, and no shock parameter is tuned.

the_architecture.node: A participant holding reserves and issuing obligations. Nodes have capacity U (resources committable), no privileged status, and no ability to create claims beyond reserves.
the_architecture.claim: An obligation from one node to another, backed at issuance by verified real reserves. A claim carries an encode fidelity D_enc = share of the claim backed by verified assets, and a decode fidelity D_dec = share of the required verifier quorum that independently confirmed the backing.
the_architecture.yield: E = U * D_enc * D_dec, with D_enc and D_dec each strictly in [0,1] so E <= U always. Dimensional bounding is enforced in code and asserted in tests.
the_architecture.full_reserve_rule: A node may not issue claims whose total exceeds its verified reserves. This is checked at issuance, not reconciled afterwards.
the_architecture.proportional_loss_rule: On a shortfall, losses are shared across claim-holders in proportion to holdings. There are no priority claims and no recourse beyond the stake.
the_architecture.multilateral_netting: THE DECENTRALISING MECHANISM. Before settlement, obligations are netted across the whole obligation graph, so offsetting positions cancel and only residual net positions require reserve movement. This is what allows a shock to be absorbed locally rather than routed through a central balance sheet.
the_architecture.verifier_quorum: A claim is admissible only if at least k independent peers verify its backing. Self-reported backing is never accepted. k is fixed at 3 before any run.
the_architecture.latency_covenant: Staged de-risking on settlement latency, carried over unchanged from the independently tested stewardship design: hold below 30 units, halve exposure between 30 and 60, exit above 60.

fixed_parameters.note: These are STRUCTURAL parameters of the mesh and apply identically to both arms wherever meaningful. No parameter takes a different value in the centralised arm than in the mesh arm. None may change after the lock.

gates.M1_the_full_reserve_invariant_holds_unde: Exhaustively exercise issuance, transfer, netting and settlement under randomised admissible operation sequences, plus adversarial ones, and assert that total claims never exceed total reserves at any intermediate state. PASS iff zero violations across at least 200,000 operations. CAN FAIL -- an implementation bug, an ordering error or a netting mistake all break it. This is a theorem about the mechanism, not an observation about the world, and it is reported as such.
gates.M2_unearned_capacity_inflation_is_detect: An attacker attempts to inflate capacity without backing, by six distinct strategies: issue-without-reserve, double-pledge the same reserve, forge verifier attestations, collude with k-1 verifiers, inflate reserves by self-report, and cycle claims through intermediaries to disguise origin. PASS iff every attack is detected AND zero honest nodes are flagged. CAN FAIL, and a single missed attack fails it. The designer does not control the outcome once the attacks are written.
gates.M3_shared_shock_replay: Replay the 4,886 real recorded debit shocks against both architectures with identical inputs and no architecture-specific constants. Measure failed settlements in each. PASS iff the mesh's failed-settlement count is strictly lower. FALSIFIABLE AND AT GENUINE RISK: netting can fail to help when the obligation graph is sparse, and a centralised balance sheet can absorb shocks a mesh cannot. A loss here is reported at full force.
gates.M4_contagion_is_bounded: Fail one node at random, 500 times, and measure how many other nodes are pushed into shortfall in each architecture. PASS iff the mesh's mean contagion count is strictly lower. CAN FAIL.
gates.M5_every_mechanism_component_earns_its_p: ABLATION. Remove multilateral netting, the verifier quorum and the latency covenant one at a time and re-run the shared-shock replay. A component earns its place iff its removal strictly worsens the mesh's failed-settlement count. PASS iff ALL THREE earn their place. FALSIFIABLE AND EXPECTED TO BE AT RISK -- in the previous ablation of an integrated design, four of seven components were dead weight. Any component that earns nothing must be NAMED as dead weight in the results, the README and the skill, never quietly retained.
gates.M6_the_meshs_cost_is_measured_not_hidden: Every decentralised design pays a coordination cost. Measure the verification overhead as the number of independent verification operations required per settled claim, and the netting computation as a share of total operations. DECLARED: the cost is expected to be strictly positive and is reported as the design's price. PASS iff the cost is measured and non-zero. falsifiable:false -- a positive cost is structurally certain, so this is a reporting obligation and is EXCLUDED from the score.
gates.M7_no_architecture_specific_constant_dif: STRUCTURAL HONESTY GATE. Inspect the parameter dictionaries actually used by each arm at run time and assert they are identical on every shared key. PASS iff no key takes a different value between arms. DECLARED falsifiable:false -- it is enforced by construction and EXCLUDED from the score. It exists so that the tuned-baseline failure mode cannot recur silently, and it is the gate the published JAX cell would fail.
gates.M8_no_theological_or_arabic_terminology_: Scan the specification, implementation and results for a fixed list of terms. PASS iff none appears. DECLARED falsifiable:false, EXCLUDED from the score, enforcing the user's terminology directive.

symmetric_null: Every count, rate and overhead is reported with its exact value whether or not it favours the mesh. M3, M4 and M5 are genuinely at risk; M1 and M2 are pass/fail properties the implementation can and might violate. M6, M7 and M8 are declared non-falsifiable and excluded from the score. No parameter or threshold in this file may move after the lock, and no result may be rescued by adding an architecture-specific constant.
what_a_pass_would_and_would_not_mean: Passing M1-M5 would establish that the mechanism, as specified, holds its reserve invariant under every operation tried, resists six named attacks, absorbs a real recorded shock sequence better than a centralised comparator under identical inputs, bounds contagion, and contains no dead components. It would NOT establish that such a system is legally permissible, economically viable, adoptable, liquid, or better than existing institutions in the world. It would NOT be empirical support: no such system has been deployed, and simulation of a design is not evidence about reality. It would establish that the design is COHERENT, ATTACK-RESISTANT AND NON-TRIVIAL -- which is the strongest honest claim available before deployment, and the claim this specification makes.
acceptance: GREEN when this spec re-hashes to its published canonical SHA-256, the shock source matches its committed hash, and every gate is evaluated exactly as written -- with misses recorded, dead components named, and the design's cost reported. Exit 0 means 'reproduces including its failures', never 'the mesh works'.
